basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 8.' and it opens 'Vers. 8. Unde scire possum quod possessurus sim eam? Quaerit signum non quasi dubitans de'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 8. Unde scire possum quod possessurus sim eam? Quaerit signum non quasi dubitans de promissione | Dei, sed modum interrogat quo hoc fieri posset. Hinc mos inolevit Judaeis ut semper signa petant, sicut Apostolus dicit: Judaei signa petunt (I Cor. I, 22).
